questiontext.text:
UniCV prototype for gap-filler questions in Python (based on python3_stage1_gapfiller, with its own interface and fixes). The student sees a complete program with some parts replaced by gaps and fills them in; the program is then run with each test case.

How to write a question

  1. Put the complete program in the Global extra field and replace each part the student must write with a gap (below). Alternatively, leave Global extra without gaps and write the code with the gaps in the Test code of every test case (test-case mode, chosen automatically): the student sees the code of the first test case, and their answers are put into the gaps of every test case, so each test can use different data (e.g. a different list). All the test cases must have the same number of gaps.
  2. Fill in the Answer with the interface (the correct gap contents) and add the test cases: Standard input and Expected output. Tick Use as example on one or two tests so that the student sees an example run above the code.
  3. Save with Validate on save ticked: the answer must pass all tests.

Kinds of gap

  • {[20]}: a text gap 20 characters wide that grows as the student types; {[10-30]}: width 10, at most 30 characters.
  • {[select: % | // | /]}: a list of choices.
  • {[drop: n | i | total]}: a gap filled from the word bank, by dragging a word or by clicking the gap and then the word. The bank shows the words of all the drop gaps together, in alphabetical order, so list wrong words (distractors) in them too.
  • Any gap can end with a hint for the student: {[20 :: The remainder of a division]}, {[select: % | // :: Think of even numbers]}.

What the student gets

  • Line numbers and syntax colours, the number of gaps filled, Tab or Enter to go to the next gap and a Clear all gaps button.
  • Before running, empty gaps, invalid choices, proscribed strings and syntax errors are reported; the gap with the error is marked in red with the message beside it. The whole program is compiled with the gaps filled in, so a gap like if x > 0 (with the colon in the code) is accepted.

Limitations

  • In test-case mode, do not tick Use as example: the example would show the code with the gaps still empty.
  • Gaps are single-line: a gap cannot hold several lines of code.
  • Inside {[ ... ]} do not use :: (it starts the hint) or ]} (it closes the gap), and the options of a select or drop gap cannot contain |.
  • An empty gap is always rejected, so the correct answer cannot be an empty gap.
  • The checks are done in steps: if a gap is empty, holds an invalid choice or a proscribed string, those errors are reported first; a syntax error in another gap is only reported at the next Check.
  • The syntax colours are a simple approximation of Python's and are applied to each piece of code between gaps separately.
  • Students' answers are stored as the list of the gaps' contents. If the gaps of a question are changed after students have answered it, their earlier answers no longer match the gaps: they get a message asking them to tell the teacher.

Differences from python3_stage1_gapfiller

  • The place of the gaps (Global extra or the test cases) is detected automatically, so the UI parameter ui_source is not needed (the html interface does not accept it). To reuse a question of the types python3_stage1_gapfiller or python3_gapfiller_demo, change its type, empty its UI parameters field and save; the gaps and the answer are read as they are.
  • The interface is new (UI plugin html): choice gaps, word bank, hints, line numbers and colours, the gap count, Clear all gaps and errors marked on their gap. Gaps written for the old interface ({[20]}, {[10-30]}) work unchanged, and answers given with the old interface (a plain list) are still read correctly by the grader.
  • echostandardinput can now be set in the template parameters (before, it was always on and could not be changed).
  • proscribedsubstrings is empty by default (before: [";", "print", "import"]), so print can be used in a gap unless the question forbids it.
  • Syntax is checked on the whole program with the gaps filled in, not on each gap alone, and the error names the gap; empty gaps are reported.
  • When the number of answers does not match the number of gaps, a clear message is shown instead of an internal error.
  • Lower limits: 20 s of CPU time and a total timeout of 20 s per check (before 50 s), and the server's default memory limit (before 1500 MB).
  • The demonstration images and data file of the original prototype were removed, which makes the prototype about ten times smaller and every check faster.

Note on input(): by default input() behaves as on the keyboard, so the prompt and the value read (followed by a new line) appear in the output and must be in the Expected output. For example, with n = int(input("n? ")) and input 4 the output starts with n? 4. Set echostandardinput to false to get plain Python behaviour (prompt without the value).

Template parameters (all optional)

  • echostandardinput (default true): see the note on input() above.
  • proscribedsubstrings (default []): strings that no gap may contain, e.g. ["print", ";"].
  • requiredsubstrings (default []): strings that must appear in at least one gap, e.g. ["for"].
  • proscribedbuiltins (default ["exec", "eval"]): built-in functions the program cannot use.
  • maxfieldlength (default none): maximum number of characters in a gap.
  • parsegaps (default true): compile the completed program before running it.
  • floattolerance (default none): if set, numbers in the output are compared with this absolute or relative tolerance.
  • strictwhitespace (default true): if false, differences in spaces are ignored.
  • useanswerfortests (default false): if true, empty Expected output fields are filled by running the question's answer.
  • extra (default ""): "pretest" or "posttest" to run each test's Extra field before or after its test code.
  • prelude (default ""): code run before the program.
  • timeout (default 5) and totaltimeout (default 20): time limits in seconds per test and in total.
  • maxstringlength (default 2000): maximum length of the outputs shown in the result table.
  • usesnumpy, usesmatplotlib and imagewidth: for questions with numpy or matplotlib graphs.

Example: {"requiredsubstrings": ["%"], "proscribedsubstrings": ["print"]}

import html import locale import json import os import re import sys import py_compile from pytester import PyTester locale.setlocale(locale.LC_ALL, 'C.UTF-8') # NOTE: the following are most of the parameters from the python3_stage1 # question type, included here so that the standard python3_stage1 support # files can be used without changed. However, only the ones prefixed by # '*' can be used in this question type (without the asterisk). KNOWN_PARAMS = { 'abortonerror': True, 'allowglobals': True, 'allownestedfunctions': False, 'checktemplateparams': True, '*echostandardinput': True, '*extra': '', '*floattolerance': None, 'globalextra': 'None', '*imagewidth': None, 'imports': [], 'isfunction': False, 'maxfunctionlength': 30, '*maxfieldlength': None, 'maxnumconstants': 4, 'maxoutputbytes': 10000, '*maxstringlength': 2000, 'norun': False, 'nostylechecks': True, 'notest': False, '*parsegaps': True, 'precheckers': ['pylint'], '*prelude': '', '*proscribedbuiltins': ['exec', 'eval'], 'proscribedfunctions': [], 'proscribedconstructs': [], '*proscribedsubstrings': [], 'pylintoptions': [], 'requiredconstructs': [], 'requiredfunctiondefinitions': [], 'requiredfunctioncalls': [], '*requiredsubstrings': [], 'requiretypehints': False, 'restrictedfiles': { 'disallow': ['__.*', 'prog.*', 'pytester.py'], }, 'restrictedmodules': { 'builtins': { 'onlyallow': [] }, 'imp': { 'onlyallow': [] }, 'importlib': { 'onlyallow': [] }, 'os': { 'disallow': ['system', '_exit', '_.*'] }, 'subprocess': { 'onlyallow': [] }, 'sys': { 'disallow': ['_.*'] }, }, 'runextra': False, 'stdinfromextra': False, '*strictwhitespace': True, 'stripmain': False, 'stripmainifpresent': False, 'testisbash': False, '*timeout': 5, '*totaltimeout': 20, 'suppresspassiveoutput': False, '*useanswerfortests': False, '*usesmatplotlib': False, '*usesnumpy': False, 'usesubprocess': False, 'warnifpassiveoutput': False, } GLOBAL_ERRORS = [] class GapMismatch(Exception): """The number of answers does not match the number of gaps in the question.""" class TestCase: def __init__(self, dict_rep, test_code_html=None): """Construct a testcase from a dictionary representation obtained via JSON""" self.testcode = dict_rep['testcode'] self.stdin = dict_rep['stdin'] self.expected = dict_rep['expected'] self.extra = dict_rep['extra'] self.display = dict_rep['display'] try: self.testtype = int(dict_rep['testtype']) except (KeyError, TypeError, ValueError): self.testtype = 0 self.hiderestiffail = bool(int(dict_rep['hiderestiffail'])) self.useasexample = bool(int(dict_rep['useasexample'])) self.mark = float(dict_rep['mark']) self.test_code_html = test_code_html # ================= CODE TO DO ALL TWIG PARAMETER PROCESSING =================== def process_template_params(): """Extract the template params into a global dictionary PARAMS""" global PARAMS, GLOBAL_ERRORS PARAMS = json.loads("""{{ QUESTION.parameters | json_encode | e('py') }}""") checktemplateparams = PARAMS.get('checktemplateparams', True) # Check for parameters that aren't allowed if checktemplateparams: author_params = set(PARAMS.keys()) allowed_params = set(key[1:] for key in KNOWN_PARAMS.keys() if key.startswith('*')) unknown_params = author_params - allowed_params filtered_params = [param for param in unknown_params if not param.startswith('_')] if filtered_params: GLOBAL_ERRORS.append(f"Unexpected template parameter(s): {list(sorted(filtered_params))}") # Now merge all the KNOWN_PARAMS into PARAMS for param_name, default in KNOWN_PARAMS.items(): if param_name.startswith('*'): param_name = param_name[1:] if param_name in PARAMS: param = PARAMS[param_name] if type(param) != type(default) and default is not None: GLOBAL_ERRORS.append(f"Template parameter {param_name} has wrong type (expected {type(default)})") else: PARAMS[param_name] = default if PARAMS['extra'] == 'stdin': PARAMS['stdinfromextra'] = True if PARAMS['runextra']: PARAMS['extra'] = 'pretest' # Legacy support if PARAMS['timeout'] < 2: PARAMS['timeout'] = 2 # Allow 1 extra second freeboard def update_test_cases(test_cases, outcome): """Return the updated testcases after replacing all empty expected fields with those from the given outcome's test_results which must have a column header 'Got'. Non-empty existing expected fields are left unchanged. If any errors occur, the return value will be None and the outcome parameter will have had its prologuehtml value updated to include an error message. """ try: results = outcome['testresults'] col_num = results[0].index('Got') for i in range(len(test_cases)): if test_cases[i].expected.strip() == '': test_cases[i].expected = results[i + 1][col_num] except ValueError: outcome['prologuehtml'] = "No 'Got' column in result table from which to get testcase expecteds" test_cases = None except Exception as e: outcome['prologuehtml'] = "Unexpected error ({}) extracting testcase expecteds from sample answer output".format(e) test_cases = None return test_cases def get_expecteds_from_answer(params, test_cases, ui_source, answer_field_values): """Run all tests using the sample answer rather than the student answer. Fill in the expected field of each test case using the sample answer and return the updated test case list. Return None if the sample answer gave any sort of runtime error """ # Insert answer fields into test cases. answer_test_cases = get_test_cases(ui_source, answer_field_values) new_params = {key: value for key, value in params.items()} new_params['IS_PRECHECK'] = False new_params['nostylechecks'] = True new_params['STUDENT_ANSWER'] = get_student_answer(ui_source, answer_field_values) new_params['running_sample_answer'] = True tester = PyTester(new_params, answer_test_cases) outcome = tester.test_code() if 'prologuehtml' in outcome: outcome['prologuehtml'] = "

ERROR IN QUESTION'S SAMPLE ANSWER. PLEASE REPORT

\n" + outcome['prologuehtml'] return outcome, None else: return outcome, update_test_cases(test_cases, outcome) # ================= CODE TO DO GAPFILLER STUFF =================== def get_test_cases(ui_source, field_values): """Return an array of Test objects from the template parameter TESTCASES""" test_cases = [] tests = json.loads("""{{ TESTCASES | json_encode | e('py') }}""") for test in tests: # If gaps come from test cases then we fill student answer into gaps. if ui_source == 'test0' and test['testcode'].strip() != '': test_code_html = insert_fields(htmlize(test['testcode']), field_values, highlight=True) test['testcode'] = insert_fields(test['testcode'], field_values) test_case = TestCase(test, test_code_html=test_code_html) else: test_case = TestCase(test) test_cases.append(test_case) return test_cases GAP_SPLITTER = r"\{\[.*?\]\}" def insert_fields(code, fields, splitter=GAP_SPLITTER, highlight=False, gap_lines=None): """Expand the given code by inserting the given fields into it, after splitting it with the given regular expression. If highlight is true, each inserted value is wrapped in a element with a blue-grey background. If gap_lines is a list, the (first, last) line numbers that each gap occupies in the result are appended to it. """ bits = re.split(splitter, code) if len(bits) != len(fields) + 1: raise GapMismatch() prog = bits[0] for i, value in enumerate(fields, 1): if len(value.splitlines()) > 1: # Indent all lines in a textarea by the indent of the first line indent = len(prog.splitlines()[-1]) if prog.splitlines() else 0 value_bits = value.splitlines() for j in range(1, len(value_bits)): value_bits[j] = indent * ' ' + value_bits[j] value = '\n'.join(value_bits) + '\n' if gap_lines is not None: first = prog.count('\n') + 1 gap_lines.append((first, first + value.rstrip('\n').count('\n'))) if highlight: value = f"{value}" prog += value + bits[i] return prog GAP_RE = re.compile(r"\{\[(.*?)\]\}") def gap_specs(code): """The kind of each gap in the code: ('text', []), ('select', options) or ('drop', words). Any gap may end with ':: hint'. """ specs = [] for m in GAP_RE.finditer(code): spec = m.group(1).split('::')[0].strip() kind = re.match(r'(?i)(select|drop)\s*:?', spec) if kind: options = [o.strip() for o in spec[kind.end():].split('|') if o.strip()] specs.append((kind.group(1).lower(), options)) else: specs.append(('text', [])) return specs def gapped_source(ui_source): """The code with the gaps, as written by the question author.""" if ui_source == 'test0': tests = json.loads("""{{ TESTCASES | json_encode | e('py') }}""") return tests[0]['testcode'] if tests else '' return """{{ QUESTION.globalextra | e('py') }}""" def read_fields(text): """The contents of the gaps: the interface stores them as a JSON list in its field 'gaps'; the ace_gapfiller interface gives the list itself. """ try: data = json.loads(text) if text.strip() else [] if isinstance(data, dict): inner = (data.get('gaps') or [''])[0] data = json.loads(inner) if inner else [] return [str(v) for v in data] if isinstance(data, list) else [] except (ValueError, TypeError, AttributeError): return [] def get_student_answer(ui_source, field_values): """Gets what should be considered the 'student answer'. If global extra is being used as the UI source, the student answer is the global extra with all the various gaps filled in. The tests then follow that code. However, if test0 is the UI source, the student answer is empty (apart from a possibly spurious module docstring) as the tests will all have had the test0 gap contents plugged into them too. """ if ui_source == 'test0': return "'''docstring'''" else: return insert_fields("""{{ QUESTION.globalextra | e('py')}}""", field_values) def snip(field, maxlen=20): """Return the given field, snipped to a max of maxlen chars""" field = ' '.join(field.split()) return field if len(field) <= maxlen else field[0:maxlen] + '...' def syntax_check(ui_source, field_values): """Compile the whole program with the gaps filled in, so that each gap is checked in its context. Returns a list of (gap number or None, message). """ gap_lines = [] program = insert_fields(gapped_source(ui_source), field_values, gap_lines=gap_lines) try: compile(program, '', 'exec') except SyntaxError as e: line = e.lineno or 0 gap = next((i for i, (first, last) in enumerate(gap_lines, 1) if first <= line <= last), None) if gap is None: # The error shows up after the gap that caused it (e.g. a missing bracket). before = [i for i, (first, last) in enumerate(gap_lines, 1) if last <= line] gap = before[-1] if before else None detail = e.msg or 'invalid syntax' if gap is not None: return [(gap, f"syntax error ({detail})")] return [(None, f"Syntax error in line {line} ({detail})")] return [] def fields_precheck(ui_source, field_values): """Checks that no gap is empty, that choice and word-bank gaps hold one of their options, field lengths, proscribed and required strings and, if the 'parsegaps' parameter is true, the syntax of the completed program. Returns a list of (gap number or None, message). """ errors = [] specs = gap_specs(gapped_source(ui_source)) bank = {w for kind, options in specs if kind == 'drop' for w in options} for i, field in enumerate(field_values, 1): kind, options = specs[i - 1] if i <= len(specs) else ('text', []) if not field.strip(): errors.append((i, "this gap is empty")) continue if kind == 'select' and field not in options: errors.append((i, "choose one of the options")) continue if kind == 'drop' and bank and field not in bank: errors.append((i, "use a word from the word bank")) continue if PARAMS['maxfieldlength'] is not None and len(field) > PARAMS['maxfieldlength']: errors.append((i, f"too long (maximum {PARAMS['maxfieldlength']} characters)")) for bad in PARAMS['proscribedsubstrings']: if bad in field: errors.append((i, f"'{bad}' is not allowed here")) for reqd in PARAMS['requiredsubstrings']: if not any(reqd in field for field in field_values): errors.append((None, f"Your answer must use '{reqd}'")) if not errors and PARAMS['parsegaps']: errors = syntax_check(ui_source, field_values) return errors def errors_html(errors): """The precheck errors as HTML. Each error in a gap also carries a marker that the question's interface reads to show it on that gap. """ lines = [] markers = '' for gap, message in errors: if gap is None: lines.append(message) else: lines.append(f"Gap {gap}: {message}") markers += (f'' f'{html.escape(message)}') return '

' + htmlize('\n'.join(lines)) + '

' + markers def htmlize(message): """An html version of the given error message""" return '
' + html.escape(message) + '
' if message else '' def process_global_params(ui_source, field_values): """Plug the globals STUDENT_ANSWER, IS_PRECHECK and QUESTION_PRECHECK into the global PARAMS """ PARAMS['STUDENT_ANSWER'] = get_student_answer(ui_source, field_values) + '\n' PARAMS['SEPARATOR'] = "##" PARAMS['IS_PRECHECK'] = "{{ IS_PRECHECK }}" == "1" PARAMS['QUESTION_PRECHECK'] = {{ QUESTION.precheck }} # Type of precheck: 0 = None, 1 = Empty etc PARAMS['ALL_OR_NOTHING'] = "{{ QUESTION.allornothing }}" == "1" # Whether or not all-or-nothing grading is being used PARAMS['GLOBAL_EXTRA'] = """{{ QUESTION.globalextra | e('py') }}\n""" def choose_ui_source(): """Where the code with the gaps is: 'globalextra' if Global extra has gaps, otherwise 'test0' if the code of the first test case has gaps (then the gaps are filled in the code of every test case). """ if GAP_RE.search("""{{ QUESTION.globalextra | e('py') }}"""): return 'globalextra' tests = json.loads("""{{ TESTCASES | json_encode | e('py') }}""") if tests and GAP_RE.search(tests[0]['testcode']): return 'test0' return 'globalextra' # Get fields and the source of the gaps. ui_source = choose_ui_source() field_values = read_fields(""" {{ STUDENT_ANSWER | e('py') }}""") answer_field_values = read_fields(""" {{ QUESTION.answer | e('py') }}""") try: process_template_params() test_cases = get_test_cases(ui_source, field_values) process_global_params(ui_source, field_values) if GLOBAL_ERRORS: errors = [(None, e) for e in GLOBAL_ERRORS] else: errors = fields_precheck(ui_source, field_values) if errors: prologue = errors_html(errors) prologue += '

Please correct the gaps marked in red and try again.

' outcome = {'fraction': 0, "prologuehtml": prologue} else: # For gap filler we don't want to apply proscribedsubstrings to all code, only the gaps as above. # We also turn off all standard style checks. PARAMS['proscribedsubstrings'] = [] PARAMS['nostylechecks'] = True PARAMS['stylechecks'] = False # For the future! if PARAMS['useanswerfortests']: outcome, test_cases = get_expecteds_from_answer(PARAMS, test_cases, ui_source, answer_field_values) if test_cases: tester = PyTester(PARAMS, test_cases) outcome = tester.test_code() except GapMismatch: outcome = {'fraction': 0, 'prologuehtml': '

The number of answers does not match the number of gaps ' 'in the question. Please tell your teacher (the gaps of the question may have been changed ' 'after this answer was given).

'} print(json.dumps(outcome))
